messages.subject: Emacs+ Keyboard Scheme in StatET Console
messages.subject_clean: Emacs+ Keyboard Scheme in StatET Console
messages.body_plain:
Dear StatET Users,

I am asking this here in case anyone was as desperate as I was to get
Emacs keybindings into Eclipse . Ignore otherwise.

I tried the emacs+ keyboard scheme [1].

After reading a discussion on their ML [2], I installed a beta version
(targeted at Juno) on my Eclipse Kepler installation - there were
posts that indicate related bugfixes in Kepler that benefit Emacs+.

With this keybinding scheme selected, my StatET Console shortcuts are
messed up badly. StatET source code editing (for me) is much enhanced
though (muscle memory and all).

The actual question: How can I let StatET Console keyboard shortcuts
fall back to StatET Editor ones? Is this even possible/recommended?

Any hints/tips much appreciated.

Best Regards,
Michael

[1] http://www.mulgasoft.com/emacsplus
[2] https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/emacsplus/k-B6y0Nv248

messages.body_plain:
Hi Michael,

Michael Bach wrote [2013-07-03 13:46]:
> Dear StatET Users,
>
> I am asking this here in case anyone was as desperate as I was to get
> Emacs keybindings into Eclipse . Ignore otherwise.
>
> I tried the emacs+ keyboard scheme [1].
>
> After reading a discussion on their ML [2], I installed a beta version
> (targeted at Juno) on my Eclipse Kepler installation - there were
> posts that indicate related bugfixes in Kepler that benefit Emacs+.
>
> With this keybinding scheme selected, my StatET Console shortcuts are
> messed up badly. StatET source code editing (for me) is much enhanced
> though (muscle memory and all).
>
> The actual question: How can I let StatET Console keyboard shortcuts
> fall back to StatET Editor ones? Is this even possible/recommended?

It seems you already understood the keyboard contexts. The StatET 
Console extends the Editing StatET context, which extends the general 
Editing context. So if you or the plug-in changes keybinding in the 
general Editing context, the mentioned context of StatET are affected too.

I have no experience with Emacs/Emacs+ keybindings. Therefore I didn't 
add special keyboard bindings in StatET for the Emacs scheme.
Nevertheless, if you have proposals for good keybindings in the console 
(or other parts of StatET) for the Emacs scheme, they are welcome, and I 
will try to integrate it in StatET.

Regards,
Stephan


>

messages.subject: auto-complete in editor
messages.body_plain:
Hello dear other users,

I have a question for the using of the auto-completion. It works fine in
the console and complete any object. With an data.frame I get after the
insert the $ sign a list of all fields.

But in the editor this don't work. After the $ appears nothing, if I
press Ctrl-space (in my configuration) it says only :"No default proposal".

Is this normal behaviour? Or perhaps an error in my configuration?

Thanks,

Christian



(Ubuntu 12.04, eclipse indigo sr2, statet 3.0.1.b201207190900E37w)

Hi Christian,

Christian Oswald wrote [2013-07-10 17:26]:
> Hello dear other users,
>
> I have a question for the using of the auto-completion. It works fine in
> the console and complete any object. With an data.frame I get after the
> insert the $ sign a list of all fields.
>
> But in the editor this don't work. After the $ appears nothing, if I
> press Ctrl-space (in my configuration) it says only :"No default proposal".
>
> Is this normal behaviour? Or perhaps an error in my configuration?

There was an bug in the content assistant for '$' proposals defined in 
source files. The bug is already fixed [1], the fix will be included in 
the next release (e.g. 3.3.1).

Regards,
Stephan

customizable too.
